evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Rep launches into "let me kind of run through a couple of his information" with no time-boxed framing, no promise of dependable quote, no wait for customer agreement.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Rep asks "Are there any other top of my questions or concerns outside of the price?" — asked after already starting to confirm moving details (probing has begun). Customer answers "For now. Not much I think, yeah."
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Customer raises one concern (price higher than expected); rep never asks follow-up like 'tell me more about that' or explores the concern further. Moves straight into logistics probing.
evidence_quotes.active_listening_reflection: No summary reflection at all. Rep acknowledges the concern exists ('okay, sure. Absolutely') but never reflects back what was heard.
evidence_quotes.logistics_details_gathered: Rep covers: property type (apartments), floor/stories (second floor), room count (one bedroom at origin, two bedroom at destination), walking distance (moving right down the street), access/parking (no issues at either location). Does not explicitly ask about additional rooms or special considerations, but overall logistics are well-covered.
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Rep gives hourly rate ($196), duration range (2.5 to 3.5 hours), cost range ($490 to $668), and personalizes: 'for a move this size it usually takes around our minimum' and 'since this is all the furniture we're moving and right down the street you should fall around that minimum, which is the two and a half hours, which would be an estimated cost around $490.'
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: Rep discloses no hidden fees and mentions minimum (2.5 hours) and per-interval billing implicitly ('hour range'), but does not explicitly state the 15-minute increments or 'not a guess' commitment framing. Partial.
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_then_silence: Never asked 'Does that feel fair?' or equivalent. Customer volunteers 'that sounds better' and rep responds immediately without holding silence.
evidence_quotes.closes_the_loop: No closure statement at all for Section 5 content.
evidence_quotes.final_concerns_check: Not asked. Rep moves to booking without asking 'What's still concerning you about this move?' or equivalent.
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: Rep never asks 'Would you like our help with your move?' Booking is assumed/discussed reactively. Customer says 'Let me discuss this price with my broker and I probably will give a callback' — rep responds by confirming existing booking but never explicitly asks for the business.
evidence_quotes.booking_confirmed: Partial. Rep confirms arrival window (8:00–8:30) and addresses (moving from one apartment to another). Does not confirm date, phone number, crew size, or notes for crew about customer concerns. Customer was already booked in system from a previous quote.

top_strength: Chauntelle gathered detailed logistics information efficiently (property type, floor count, items list, access/parking) and provided a clear, personalized price anchor with a reasonable range explanation that directly addressed the customer's price concern from the prior quote.
coaching_note: Skip the quid-pro-quo framing entirely and move straight to probing — instead, front-load Section 1 with the time-boxed ask and promise of a dependable quote before any discovery, and never ask 'other concerns' after probing has already begun; also deliver both Two Promises (On-Time Guarantee and Damage Coverage) before moving to close, since this is a full sales call with pricing.
